page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Running on the Xen hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core, and includes a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline speed of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the compute and memory subsystems operate on the lower end of the spectrum. The Intel Xeon processor delivers single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance in the bottom 10%, with a PassMark CPU score categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only cached speed of 157.88 GB/sec and an uncached write speed of 14.23 GB/sec, placing memory performance in the bottom 10% to 25%. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also reflect weak to poor performance, with Redis handling 2.54 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its virtual compute resources. However, the tradeoff is a legacy CPU architecture and lower memory bandwidth, which limits its suitability for compute-intensive or high-throughput real-time processing. It represents a qualitative value for workloads that require significant local storage capacity and moderate memory without demanding high-performance CPU execution.

This instance is best suited for storage-intensive workloads that benefit from local NVMe SSDs, such as NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, and distributed file systems. It is also appropriate for moderate web serving and data caching applications where storage capacity and memory footprint are prioritized over raw computational speed.
